_meta.analysis_window: Deepest past-24h review of all 17 configured trackers plus oil/energy, IAEA/UN, NATO/allied positions, exact-slug Polymarket sanity, direct-publisher inspection, and 15 emerging-crisis candidates.
_meta.source_limitation: Source mix: official releases, reputable public reporting, public-news headline indexes, market data, and energy feeds. Upstream source coverage was degraded in this run, so the assessment uses corroborated fallback sources and treats single-source claims as watch items until confirmed.

fallbacks_used: Google News RSS (18 core + 42 targeted + 9 exact-event queries)
browser direct inspection of The National, UN News and NATO
direct official feeds/pages and terminal HTTP
direct_failures: Google News direct Reuters target did not render

signals_changed.note: No canonical active-set change. A negation-triggered pipeline false positive was removed before final publication; no evidence justified activating a new canonical signal.

auto_detection.decision: No untracked crisis met the configured three-mention/two-source gate for a distinct new escalation. A Gulf of Aden hijack appeared in one publisher relaying an inaccessible UKMTO notice; the current Myanmar Rakhine airstrike appeared in one current publisher; Haiti received a UN Security Council review but no discrete new threshold; other emerging-lane hits were absent, stale, analytical, humanitarian, or pollution from already tracked wars.

false_recency_exclusions: Taiwan stories indexed after 21Z still describe June vessel activity rather than a current force event.
The Sudan sanctions are fresh policy action, but the alleged chlorine use is not established as a same-day battlefield event.
Mali headlines remain follow-on casualty reporting on the already-scored Anefis-Gao ambush.
Second Thomas Shoal headlines remain follow-on reporting on the already-scored assault.
Pakistan-Afghanistan search pollution was excluded; the 19 July Kurram claim remains one-sided watch evidence.

allied_positions.NATO: NATO confirmed a Ukrainian request through the Euro-Atlantic Disaster Response Coordination Centre on 20 July. This is civilian emergency response, not Article 5, allied combat entry or a new force deployment against Russia.
allied_positions.UN: UN News continued to call for U.S.-Iran de-escalation, documented Ukraine aid-facility damage, and convened a Haiti Security Council review. No new UN-authorized combat action appeared.
allied_positions.IAEA: No newer verified enrichment, access, Fordow, reprocessing or test threshold surfaced; direct IAEA pages remained HTTP 403.
allied_positions.South_China_Sea: No treaty invocation, alliance consultation or new allied combat deployment followed the already-scored Second Thomas Shoal assault.

energy_oil.interpretation: Brent and WTI remained elevated versus the pre-conflict baseline but were down over 24 hours. That is consistent with severe stress without a fresh market discontinuity proving literal zero Hormuz passage or Houthi enforcement.
energy_oil.caveat: Vendor timestamps vary by instrument; market data are sanity-only and did not set tracker probabilities.

energy_sanity.interpretation: Oil stayed elevated but the negative 24-hour move did not corroborate a new chokepoint shutdown or enforced Red Sea blockade.
